# task-b0210b8b: recolor complete lines

## When to Use
Use for task-b0210b8b when a sparse patterned grid contains complete uniform rows or columns that stand out as separators/lines.

## Confirmed rule
Identify any complete horizontal row or complete vertical column whose cells all have the same color C. Recolor every cell in each such full line to color 2. Leave all other cells unchanged. If full lines intersect, recolor the intersection as 2 as part of the same operation. The dimensions remain unchanged.

## Evidence and accepted case
A demo pair (21x28) had complete rows of color 1 at rows 1, 4, and 14 (0-indexed) and complete columns of color 1 at columns 0, 5, 7, 8, 13, and 15. The output changed those complete-line cells to 2, while other occurrences of color 1 and the color-3 pattern remained unchanged.

The accepted test was 12x8 with color 5 forming full columns 2 and 3 and a complete row 9. The correct output changed exactly those cells to 2; every other cell remained unchanged. This confirms the line-recoloring operation with different line color and geometry.

## Additional accepted case
A 15x7 test had color 8 in complete rows 2 and 14 and complete column 0. The accepted output changed exactly those rows/column cells to 2, while preserving every other cell (including partial runs and isolated 8s). This further validates the rule for color 8 and intersecting horizontal/vertical lines.

## Additional accepted case: 26x23 test
A 26x23 input with background colors 5 and 9 had complete rows 9 and 25 and complete columns 9, 15, 18, and 22, all uniformly color 9. The accepted output changed exactly the union of those lines to color 2. All nonqualifying cells were unchanged. This verifies the rule on a larger grid with multiple complete rows/columns sharing line color 9.

## Application checks
- A line must span the entire grid dimension and be uniform in the same input color; do not recolor partial runs or isolated cells.
- Determine qualifying rows/columns from the original input, then recolor their union to 2.
- Preserve all nonqualifying cells, even if they share the line color.
